youtube.baslik: Can a loud sound make your head spin? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: In superior canal dehiscence, loud sound can cause vertigo or oscillopsia; this is called the Tullio phenomenon. Part of the sound energy flows not to the cochlea but through the superior canal toward the opening, deflecting the cupula and sending the brain a false spinning signal. Hearing one's own voice echo, called autophony, is also a common complaint.
